hypothesis: For one complete Qwen3.8-27B MLP projection shape, directly transcoding the canonical 189-bit 64-of-128 enumerative ternary groups into the 192-bit mask64 compute image will remain byte-identical to dense decode followed by mask64 packing while reducing peak process RSS by at least 64 MiB, using no dense 89,128,960-byte INT8 layer intermediate, finishing within five seconds, and costing no more than 1.75 times the dense control's one-time load latency on the pinned x86 CPU node

scope.reason_shapes_share_work: both shapes contain exactly 696320 groups of 128 weights
scope.input: a canonical synthetic full-shape enumerative payload with rank-zero first-half support and alternating signs
scope.claim_boundary: full-shape synthetic load-time transcode only; not real weights, model quality, token throughput, semi-lossless compression, or a scientific breakthrough

comparison.candidate: direct native enumerative-to-mask64 transcode without materializing dense ternary codes
comparison.control: frozen native enumerative decode to a dense INT8 matrix followed by the frozen native mask64 packer
comparison.timing_source: perf_counter around the complete public Python binding operation

disclosed_non_authoritative_arm64_pilot.scientific_status: engineering pilot only; not the authoritative x86 gate and not evidence of a speed improvement

a gate rejection is retained as a valid negative result and does not authorize threshold tuning
